arxiv-2109-13356.title: Efficient Computer Vision on Edge Devices with Pipeline-Parallel Hierarchical Neural Networks
arxiv-2109-13356.creator: Abhinav Goel, Caleb Tung, Xiao Hu, George K. Thiruvathukal 1 , James C. Davis, Yung-Hsiang Lu
arxiv-2109-13356.description: Abstract Computer vision on low-power edge devices enables applications including search-and-rescue and security. State-of-the-art computer vision algorithms, such as Deep Neural Networks (DNNs), are too large for inference on low-power edge devices. To improve efficiency, some existing approaches parallelize DNN inference across multiple edge devices.

arxiv-2201-03655.title: A likelihood ratio based domain adaptation method for E2E models
arxiv-2201-03655.creator: Chhavi Choudhury, Ankur Gandhe, Xiaohan Ding, Ivan Bulyko
arxiv-2201-03655.description: Abstract End-to-end (E2E) automatic speech recognition models like Recurrent Neural Networks Transducer (RNN-T) are becoming a popular choice for streaming ASR applications like voice assistants. While E2E models are very effective at learning representation of the training data they are trained on, their accuracy on unseen domains remains a challenging problem.

arxiv-2202-05849.title: Resolving Combinatorial Ambiguities in Dilepton t ​ t ¯ t\bar{t} Event Topologies with Neural Networks
arxiv-2202-05849.creator: Haider Alhazmi, Zhongtian Dong, Li Huang, Jeong Han Kim, Kyoungchul Kong, David Shih
arxiv-2202-05849.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Haider Alhazmi, Zhongtian Dong, Li Huang, Jeong Han Kim, Kyoungchul Kong, David Shih. We study the potential of deep learning to resolve the combinatorial problem in SUSY-like events with two invisible particles at the LHC. As a concrete example, we focus on dileptonic t ​ t ¯ t\bar{t} events, where the combinatorial problem becomes an issue of binary classification: pairing the correct lepton with each b b quark coming from the decays of the tops.

arxiv-2212-08214.title: Reinforcement Learning for Agile Active Target Sensing with a UAV
arxiv-2212-08214.creator: Harsh Goel, Laura Jarin Lipschitz, Saurav Agarwal, Sandeep Manjanna, Vijay Kumar
arxiv-2212-08214.description: Abstract Active target sensing is the task of discovering and classifying an unknown number of targets in an environment and is critical in search-and-rescue missions. This paper develops a deep reinforcement learning approach to plan informative trajectories that increase the likelihood for an uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) to discover missing targets.

arxiv-2312-14135.title: V ∗ : Guided Visual Search as a Core Mechanism in Multimodal LLMs
arxiv-2312-14135.creator: Penghao Wu UC San Diego pew011@ucsd.edu Saining XieNew York University saining.xie@nyu.edu
arxiv-2312-14135.description: Abstract When we look around and perform complex tasks, how we see and selectively process what we see is crucial. However, the lack of this visual search mechanism in current multimodal LLMs (MLLMs) hinders their ability to focus on important visual details, especially when handling high-resolution and visually crowded images.

arxiv-2408-01690.title: IDNet: A Novel Dataset for Identity Document Analysis and Fraud Detection

arxiv-2408-01690.description: Abstract Effective fraud detection and analysis of government-issued identity documents, such as passports, driver’s licenses, and identity cards, are essential in thwarting identity theft and bolstering security on online platforms. The training of accurate fraud detection and analysis tools depends on the availability of extensive identity document datasets.

pmc-13134517.title: Targeting Inflammation and Immune Regulation in Chronic Inflammation Associated Cancers
pmc-13134517.creator: Lawan Rabiu, Mengzhu Chinn, Feng Chen, Yerkezhan Yerkinkazhina, Yuan Tian, Wei‐Guo Zhu
pmc-13134517.description: Chronic inflammation is a fundamental driver of cancer development, linking persistent immune activation to genomic instability, microenvironmental remodeling, and malignant transformation. In inflammation‐associated malignancies such as colitis‐associated cancer (CAC) and metabolic dysfunction–associated fatty liver disease–related hepatocellular carcinoma (MAFLD‐HCC), sustained inflammatory signaling integrates tissue injury with oncogenic pathways to promote tumor initiation and progression.

pmc-13521946.title: Circularly polarized electroluminescence from topologically chiral [2]catenane-based neutral radicals with tunable deep-red emission
pmc-13521946.creator: Yu Wang, Xiao-Qin Xu, Zhiwen Gao, Xue Li, Yiming Yang, Wen-Long Zhao, Meng Li, Wei Wang, Chuan-Feng Chen, Hai-Bo Yang
pmc-13521946.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Stable organic radicals with unique luminescence have demonstrated great importance in photoelectromagnetic materials and have found broad applicability in the field of organic light-emitting diode (OLEDs). Aiming to further extend their application into chiral optoelectronic devices, by employing topologically chiral [2]catenane as the key chiral skeleton, this work presents the first successful construction of circularly polarized OLEDs (CP-OLEDs) based on donor–acceptor (D–A•) type neutral tris(2,4,6-trichlorophenyl)methyl (TTM) radicals.
